original_question: For the polynomial sequences A_n(t) and A_tilde_n(t) associated with the modified multiple-zeta-value identity in Section 7, can these polynomials be expressed explicitly in hypergeometric form?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Questions 7.1 (the second question): whether the polynomial sequences A_n(t) and A_tilde_n(t) attached to the modified multiple-zeta-value identity can be given in an explicit hypergeometric form.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the right section of the paper, the correct polynomial families A_n(t) and A_tilde_n(t), their connection with the modified multiple-zeta-value identity, and the specific part of the open problem asking for an explicit hypergeometric description.
missing_details: The exact official target is only the second part of Questions 7.1; the paper also asks a separate first question about deducing the limit of A_tilde_n(t) from recurrence (7.1), and that should not be merged into this question.
A_n(t) must be defined explicitly by the recurrence (n^3 - (-1)^n t^3)A_n(t) + (n+1)^2(2n+1)A_{n+1}(t) + (n+2)^2(n+1)A_{n+2}(t) = 0 together with the initial conditions A_0(t)=1 and A_1(t)=0.
A_tilde_n(t) is not an independent family in the paper; it is defined by A_tilde_n(t) = sum_{k=0}^n A_k(t).
The paper also records an equivalent recurrence for A_tilde_n(t), namely (n^3 - (-1)^n t^3)A_tilde_{n-1}(t) + n(2n+1)A_tilde_n(t) - n(n+1)^2 A_tilde_{n+1}(t) = 0, with the index range n >= 1.
The ambient ring is Q[t^3]; equivalently, the polynomials are to be viewed as polynomials in the variable x = t^3.
The paper explicitly states that A_n(t) has degree floor(n/2) in x = t^3; the draft omits this degree datum.
The quantifier should be made explicit: the question concerns the whole sequence, i.e. all n >= 0.
To stay paper-faithful, the question should ask for explicit closed hypergeometric formulas, not merely generating functions, asymptotics, or representations of the limiting infinite product.
refined_question: In Section 7's modified multiple-zeta-value setting, let A_n(t) in Q[t^3] be the polynomial sequence defined for n >= 0 by A_0(t)=1, A_1(t)=0, and (n^3 - (-1)^n t^3)A_n(t) + (n+1)^2(2n+1)A_{n+1}(t) + (n+2)^2(n+1)A_{n+2}(t) = 0, where A_n(t) has degree floor(n/2) in x=t^3; and let A_tilde_n(t) = sum_{k=0}^n A_k(t) (equivalently, A_tilde_n satisfies (n^3 - (-1)^n t^3)A_tilde_{n-1}(t) + n(2n+1)A_tilde_n(t) - n(n+1)^2 A_tilde_{n+1}(t) = 0 for n >= 1). Can one find explicit hypergeometric formulas for A_n(t) and A_tilde_n(t) for every n >= 0?
justification: This rewrite matches the paper's actual open problem in the narrowest official form available: the second question in Questions 7.1. It is made stand-alone by importing exactly the nearby definitions and assumptions that the paper uses immediately before posing the question: the recurrence and initial data for A_n(t), the fact that A_n(t) lies in Q[t^3] and has degree floor(n/2) in x=t^3, and the definition (plus equivalent recurrence) of A_tilde_n(t). It does not broaden the problem to the separate first question of Questions 7.1 about proving the limit of A_tilde_n(t), and it does not pull in the neighboring discussion of zero distributions except as background context.
